name: Maurrassisme
summary: Maurrassisme is the doctrine of Charles Maurras and Action française: an integral nationalism holding that France can be restored only through a hereditary, anti-parliamentary and decentralized monarchy. It puts politics first, rejects democracy, liberalism and the Revolution, values Catholicism as social order rather than as faith, and treats Jews, Protestants, Freemasons and foreigners as 'anti-France'.
scope: Maurras's doctrine as set out in Enquête sur la monarchie (1900) and the Action française movement from 1899 to about 1945, including its corporatist and national-syndicalist leanings and its support of Vichy. Excludes later neo-Maurrassian groups; modern questions are inferred.

sources.title: Charles Maurras
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Antisemitism, anti-democracy, anti-capitalism and anti-communism, violence, war and foreign policy, Vichy.

sources.title: Action française
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Movement doctrine: corporatism, national syndicalism, Catholicism as state religion, Camelots du Roi, coup aims, Vatican condemnation.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Maurras's sources say nothing on health care; a paternal monarchy could fund it, but no stated doctrine commits adherents either way.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage policy is not discussed in the sources; corporatist bodies would set wages rather than statute, so adherents have no clear line.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Maurras is described as opposed to capitalism and as corporatist and dirigiste, so he would not trust markets over state and corporate direction.

public-ownership.rationale: Dirigiste but corporatist rather than nationalizing; no source states a view on public ownership of utilities, so this is inferred.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Tax policy is not documented; anti-capitalist rhetoric is offset by his defence of hereditary patrimony, so no clear lean.

unions-good.rationale: Action française took up national syndicalism and corporations but opposed class-struggle unionism, so adherents split on unions as such.

property-fundamental.rationale: The hereditary dynasty and family patrimony are central to his case, from which respect for property is inferred; he does not discuss property rights directly.

regulate-corporations.rationale: As a dirigiste corporatist who opposed capitalism, he would favor state oversight of business, though the sources give no specifics.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; a paternalist and corporatist outlook neither endorses welfare cuts nor a large welfare state.

worker-ownership.rationale: He opposed communism and class politics; corporatist cooperation between owners and workers keeps existing ownership, an inference rather than a stated position.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Strong authority and security of the state against internal enemies is central, so he would accept it; counter-terrorism surveillance is anachronistic.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not discussed; his order-and-tradition outlook points against legalization.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: He was himself convicted of incitement against Jewish politicians and would see republican speech law as a partisan tool, though he wanted the 'anti-France' suppressed.

strong-leader.rationale: Enquête sur la monarchie demands a king who reigns and governs, freed from the yoke of deputies; he would accept councils, but not parliamentary gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: He wants a strong state with authority at the top; anarchism is the opposite of his doctrine.

empower-police-military.rationale: His authoritarian nationalism backed order and the military, and his Camelots du Roi acted as a paramilitary force.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from his Catholic-conservative social order.

decide-locally.rationale: One of the four principles of his monarchy is decentralization: the king at the top with local and regional liberties below.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; his emphasis on authority and order suggests punishment first.

traditional-family.rationale: The family appears with locality, work and parish as part of the pays réel on which he wanted society to rest.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from his traditionalist, Catholic-aligned social order.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from his support for Catholic social order and traditional family.

more-religion-public.rationale: He prized Catholicism as a social glue though agnostic himself, and the movement backed restoring it as state religion after 1905.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anachronistic; his nationalism and opposition to egalitarianism point against such programs.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from traditionalism and natural inequality.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He judges French questions from the standpoint of France and finds no political framework wider than the nation; tradition is the heart of his doctrine.

gradual-change.rationale: Organizing empiricism: institutions should come from centuries of experience, though he accepted a coup to restore the monarchy.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He classed foreigners (métèques) among the 'anti-France'; immigration levels as such are not discussed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He holds that no political framework exists wider than the nation and attacked humanitarian utopianism.

free-trade.rationale: Anti-liberal and dirigiste; inferred, no explicit trade statement in sources.

nation-first.rationale: The nation is the sole political frame and 'France d'abord' was his guiding line, including under Vichy.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: He condemned 'l'utopie humanitaire' and put national interest first.

open-borders.rationale: His doctrine excludes foreigners as anti-France and rests on rooted national community.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis in the doctrine.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; his empiricism neither celebrates nor rejects technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; national power and independence suggest mild support.

revolution-justified.rationale: He blamed the 1789 Revolution for France's decline and was counter-revolutionary, though he planned a royalist coup.

experts-over-public.rationale: His rejection of democracy in favour of natural hierarchy implies deference to competent rulers and councils.

central-planning.rationale: Dirigiste but corporatist and anti-communist; no support for full central planning is documented.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred from his opposition to both capitalism and communism, which does not favor worker or public ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land taxation is not part of Maurras's writings, and his corporatist order gives no lead on tax design, so adherents have no position.

tax-inheritance.rationale: His case for heredity extends to families passing on a patrimony; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Anachronistic; unconditional state payments don't fit his corporatist order.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Dirigiste economic nationalism suggests protection; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Described as dirigiste; specific investment policy is not documented.

widespread-small-property.rationale: His organic society of trades, families and localities favors broad rooted ownership, but he did not state it.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: He was staunchly opposed to communism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; a state-directed order is inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Corporatism is named in his doctrine and Enquête sur la monarchie refers readers to La Tour du Pin's corporatist writings for the social order.

one-party-rule.rationale: He wanted a hereditary king, not a ruling party, and the League was a pressure movement, not a state party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary monarchy is the keystone of his doctrine; heredity ties the dynasty's interest to the nation's.

democracy-best.rationale: He rejected democratic principles as contrary to natural inequality and blamed democracy for national decline.

direct-votes.rationale: He rejected popular sovereignty and democracy; local and corporate representation was his only accepted form.

workers-councils.rationale: Opposed to communism and class-based rule; the base would be family, locality and trade under a king.

right-to-secede.rationale: He wanted regional liberties inside a unified France under the king, not secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: He held democracy contradicts natural inequality and defended dynastic rule trained from childhood.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Camelots du Roi practised street violence and he theorized a coup d'état and called for killings of opponents.

war-builds-character.rationale: He supported entry into World War I and revanchism but sources don't state war as character-building.

separate-church-state.rationale: The movement backed restoring Catholicism as state religion after the 1905 separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: His politics rested on reason, tradition and natural law, with Catholicism valued as social order rather than revelation.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A strong centralized royal authority over justice and defence is part of his model.

military-superiority.rationale: He was hostile to Germany, demanded a harsh Versailles, and backed national strength.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He rejected scientific racism and defined the nation by history and tradition, though he excluded Jews, Protestants, Freemasons and foreigners.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He rejected communism and class struggle in favour of national solidarity under the king.

equal-outcomes.rationale: His doctrine centres on natural inequality and hierarchy.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Anachronistic; his national sovereignty framework disfavors it.

civilizational-union.rationale: He recognised no framework wider than the nation, though a Latin or Catholic civilizational sympathy existed.

self-interest-moral.rationale: His organic view puts national and corporate duties above individualism, though he never addressed the claim directly.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rejected abstract individual rights for organic duties to family, locality, trade and nation as in the pays réel.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental value questions are outside the doctrine; his rooted love of land and locality does not decide the philosophical point.

limit-population.rationale: Nationalists of this era feared depopulation; not specifically documented.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed; he blamed the Revolution and liberalism, not industry.

accelerate-technology.rationale: His empiricism and respect for tradition disfavor disruptive change; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; personal royal authority is his model.

restore-past-order.rationale: He held France had declined since 1789 and wanted the monarchy back; his restoration is organizing empiricism, though framed as renewal.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Organizing empiricism: institutions are judged by historical experience, not abstract theory, though he was doctrinaire.

direct-action.rationale: He theorized leagues and extra-parliamentary action, including a coup, instead of elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: He accepted violent and coercive means for a restored order.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Opposed to a rupture with tradition and civilization; classical and Catholic culture is his ideal.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: His corporatist order rests on trades and hierarchy.

production-for-use.rationale: Opposed to communism; corporatist order is not use-based planning.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist exploitation theory contradicts his rejection of class struggle.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He was staunchly opposed to communism and to class rule.

collective-farming.rationale: Rooted local and family ownership is closer to his pays réel; collectivism is rejected as communism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist theory is rejected; he attributed war to republican weakness and German power.

taxation-theft.rationale: He wanted a strong state, with assemblies consenting to taxes.

harm-principle.rationale: His authoritarian traditionalism allows the state to enforce moral and national order.

individual-rights-only.rationale: His organic view of communities and the nation rejects individualist rights.

conscription.rationale: He backed national defence and the military against Germany.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Exit is incompatible with his rooted, nation-first outlook.

state-as-business.rationale: Rejects a customer model of the state; the state is an organic patrimony.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; his regional liberties are of a different type.

media-academia-power.rationale: His 'legal country' critique targeted republican elites and press; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: He rejected scientific racism, so he would not ground ability in race.

organic-representation.rationale: Enquête sur la monarchie wants councils and assemblies of corporations, family and locality, and refers to La Tour du Pin's corporatism.

total-state.rationale: His monarchy decentralizes and leaves local and corporate liberties; authority is strong but not total.

national-rebirth.rationale: He held France was in decline since 1789 and the monarchy would restore national greatness.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He opposed colonial expansion as a distraction from Germany, so not clear.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on a hereditary dynasty and law, not feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Not part of his corporatist order.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: He appealed to natural order and reason.

universal-morality.rationale: He appealed to natural law but made nationalism the horizon.

single-common-good.rationale: He held that the nation's good is a single end of politics, set against party competition.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He classed Jews as 'anti-France' but his view of a Jewish state is not documented.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Maurras never addressed diaspora return, and his French focus gives no basis for a rule, so this is a neutral inference.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival was not a Maurrassian theme, though his Provençal regionalism could cut either way, so he is left neutral.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democracy rejected; corporatist bodies and authority instead.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not documented; the movement founded its own higher education institute.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Budget and stimulus policy was not part of his political writing, and nothing in the doctrine decides it.

rule-by-example.rationale: He wanted a trained heir, but also laws and councils.

national-self-determination.rationale: He held each nation as the sole political frame, but his stance on other peoples is not documented.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; he put national interest first.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The monarchy is presented as a theorem, scientific and reasoned, not revealed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditionality is not discussed; a paternalist order might favor it but corporatist solidarity could oppose it, so it is neutral.

class-collaboration.rationale: He called for national solidarity and corporatism opposing class struggle, with the king as keystone.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Tradition and inherited institutions are valued.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his Europeanist nationalism.

workers-nation.rationale: Action française combined integral nationalism with national syndicalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed explicitly; inferred from traditionalism.

ban-interest.rationale: He attacked finance rhetorically but sources record no demand for banning interest; this is inferred as a mild disagreement.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He rejected scientific racism, though he favored state action against the Jews as a group.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is anachronistic for Maurras, and nothing in the doctrine decides it, so a neutral low-confidence answer.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: He regarded foreigners as anti-France; assimilation is not documented.

elite-replacement.rationale: Replacement theory is later; he distrusted Jews and foreigners but his thought centred on republican elites.

national-mission.rationale: He wanted France restored for itself rather than spreading its government abroad, and opposed colonial adventure as a diversion, leaving this neutral.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He attacked the Republic's politicians as putting party above nation, the pays légal against the pays réel.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not documented; Catholic-aligned traditionalism points against.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: He defended state authority and the army and was hostile to republican retribution, so adherents would resist such accountability; this is inferred.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: He rejected scientific racism; excluded groups by 'anti-France'.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Held to natural inequality; though Christian equal worth was valued.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anachronistic question; Maurras backed France's empire in some respects but his sources record no view on settler colonialism, so a mild inferred disagreement.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Uniform civil law across religions is not discussed; he favored regional liberties but a single French law is also plausible, so neutral.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religious conversion rules are not addressed; he valued Catholicism socially but was personally agnostic, so neutral.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A question from Indian politics that his doctrine never touched; inferred disagreement from traditional French practice.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The movement backed restoring Catholic position, opposing laïque schooling.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Legitimacy rests on reason and heredity, not popular sovereignty or social contract.

population-transfer.rationale: He supported state anti-Semitism and criticized Vichy's 1940 Jewish statute as too moderate.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: He backed street violence and a coup.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social-Darwinist competition between peoples was not his framework; he stressed order, tradition and cooperation, and sources do not decide it.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: He accepted state repression of the 'anti-France' and himself was repressed under the Republic.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican theory of non-domination is not engaged by Maurras, who rejected the republican tradition, so a weak inferred disagreement.

separated-powers.rationale: He wanted a king who reigns and governs, not checks by deputies, though councils would provide advice and consent.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Corporatist solidarity and paternal duty suggest concern for workers, but no source gives the poor priority in law, so neutral.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing policy is not addressed in his sources, so neutral.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Corporatism seeks to replace conflict between classes by corporate bodies.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not part of his analysis, which blamed political institutions rather than demography.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: His exclusion of Jews, Protestants, Freemasons and foreigners rested on cohesion.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He supported strong authority against internal enemies and backed Vichy.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Dirigiste instincts could favor it, but no source documents price control views, so neutral.

party-controls-media.rationale: He wanted royal authority, not a ruling party; he himself was subject to press censorship.

party-commands-army.rationale: The army would be under the king.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: He wanted councils and assemblies under a king, not pay rules for representatives, so there is nothing to answer.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: He opposed party politics itself, but internal party discipline is not discussed, so neutral.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: No political framework wider than the nation.

head-commands-forces.rationale: A king who reigns and governs, as in the Enquête, commands the state including the army.

clerical-rule.rationale: Maurras was agnostic and valued the Church as an instrument for national order, not as a ruler.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: He supported union nationale in 1914 and 1940.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not documented; inferred from authoritarian traditionalism.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: A hereditary king serves for life.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He supported alliance diplomacy against Germany.

people-in-arms.rationale: He favored a disciplined national army under the crown; an armed citizenry militia is not a documented preference, so a mild disagreement.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The pays réel of locality, parish, family.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: His critique targeted the republican political class rather than university graduates, and he was himself an intellectual, so neutral.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: He held France and the classical tradition higher.

death-penalty.rationale: Not documented directly, but he advocated violence against opponents and authority.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: His nation is built on historic continuity, but he did not state a citizenship rule.

minority-language-support.rationale: As a Provençal regionalist he valued regional cultural liberties.

religious-exemptions.rationale: He excluded minorities like Protestants as anti-France.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Social cohesion and tradition are prized.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International development debt is not discussed in his sources; no principle decides it.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Decolonization economics is outside his doctrine; he did not see political order as needing property transformation, so a mild disagreement.

constituent-assembly.rationale: He rejected popular sovereignty; the monarchy is restored not voted in.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Rapid development is not his theme; he supported strong authority, but for national restoration rather than growth, so neutral.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Hereditary succession in place of election is his keystone.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not discussed, and a state-led order would not obviously favor independence, so neutral.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist-internal debate on which his sources are silent; he simply opposed Soviet communism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is not in his writings, so neutral.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The king above parties unifying the nation is core to his argument against partisan republic.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Legitimacy is rational not divine right.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax rate design is not addressed in the sources, so neutral.

character-from-environment.rationale: His thought stressed inheritance of tradition and natural inequality, though he also relied on upbringing in training a dynastic heir, so a weak disagreement.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He blamed Louis XIV's absolutism, wanted a king bound by councils.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic and absent from his doctrine, so neutral.

mixed-constitution.rationale: He wanted a king with councils, not strictly a mixed regime.

leader-cult.rationale: He criticized fascist cults though he valued Pétain.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family court policy is not discussed; his family emphasis cuts in no clear direction here.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist internal doctrine that Maurras, who opposed communism, would reject.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return rights are not addressed in the sources, so neutral.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: He was himself agnostic for most of his life, and his Catholicism was political rather than doctrinal, so he would not punish apostasy; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not discussed; his Catholic-traditional but French-secular cultural frame points against a legal dress mandate.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: No wider framework than the nation.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: He regarded Jews and other minorities as anti-France and did not accept their claim on equal national belonging; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: He opposed Marxism, attributing decline to politics, hence 'Politics first'.

ban-cartels.rationale: He distrusted liberal finance but his corporatist order would organize industry in bodies, not break them up, so neutral.

no-bailouts.rationale: Public rescue of firms was not addressed, and dirigisme cuts against a strict rule, so neutral.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas for sexes in public bodies contradict his traditional, hierarchical view of public life; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: International trade agreement design is not addressed in his writings, and he disliked supranational rules in any case, so neutral.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not in his writings; he valued duty and national devotion but gave no incentive system.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Camelots du Roi and the coup d'état plans.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Heredity is the keystone of the monarchy; hereditary institutions defended.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He opposed assimilationist colonialism but favored empire.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Institut d'Action française gave an alternative education.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Anachronistic; his rejection of egalitarian social engineering points weakly toward agreement.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation is not addressed in his sources, so neutral.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Maurras was no theorist of capitalist crisis, so neutral.

former-empire-influence.rationale: He supported French empire but wrote little on postcolonial influence, so neutral.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed; this is a development-economics debate outside his doctrine.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist concept; Maurras's rejection of Marxist class analysis implies disagreement.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarian private-association rights are not his framework; he favored state action against excluded groups, so a mild disagreement.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Entrenched individual rights belong to the liberal tradition he opposed, so a weak inferred disagreement.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed; a nationalist might favor stable treaties or revision, so neutral.

elective-rulers.rationale: Heredity rather than election is the keystone.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The dynasty is expected to be bound by its own interest, not popular resistance.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Organic hierarchy with duties, though not explicitly documented.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Frankfurt School theme; Maurras's culture critique blamed romanticism and the Revolution, so neutral.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim outside his doctrine, and he rejected class analysis, so a weak disagreement.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A dependency theory claim he did not hold and would reject with Marxism; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: A question internal to communist parties on which he had no stake, so neutral.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Aid dependency is not discussed; his nationalism values self-reliance but he said nothing about poor countries, so neutral.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Revanchist stance on Versailles toward Germany.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Anachronistic; his colonial views favored a French-led order, so a mild inferred disagreement.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: He opposed communism and Nazism but not the authoritarian state.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historical question that his sources never touch, so neutral.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: His reverence for inherited tradition and national history suggests keeping monuments to the past.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not discussed in his sources, so neutral.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not discussed in his sources, so neutral.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Organizing empiricism: institutions arise from a nation's own history.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Maurras's circle courted army and coup.

paid-care-work.rationale: Paying for domestic labor is a modern feminist demand; his traditional family model suggests mild disagreement.

filial-duty.rationale: Family is part of the pays réel.

office-by-exam.rationale: He did not address civil service recruitment; he favored a hereditary head and competence in councils, so neutral.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Catholic-aligned traditionalism and his family emphasis point toward restrictions on divorce; this is inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not addressed; corporatist solidarity points weakly against individual accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: He valued rooted inheritance of land and family property, which conflicts with state-ownership-only tenure; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Enquête wants assemblies consenting to taxes but not parliamentary governments.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: A modern legal doctrine of egalitarian anti-discrimination that his outlook would reject; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: He supported alliances and national interest, but covert war policy is not documented, so neutral.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Intervention within a bloc is a Cold War question his sources never reach, so neutral.

corporate-influence.rationale: He was anti-capitalist and attacked the Republic's financial and political elites, which supports agreement that business sways government.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: His hostility to foreign influence in French affairs suggests support, but the matter is anachronistic.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Nationalists of his era feared depopulation and valued the family, so state incentives are a reasonable inference.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local property rules are not addressed; his regionalism and hostility to foreigners push slightly either way, so neutral.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employment policy is not in the sources, so neutral.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: His doctrine rests on authority, order and tradition, so a denial of any duty to obey law contradicts it.

non-intervention.rationale: Not addressed in general terms; he supported intervention in his nation's interest but not on principle, so neutral.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not addressed; corporatism organizes by trade or corporation, so neutral.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: He grouped Jews, Protestants, Freemasons and foreigners as the confederated states of 'anti-France' and linked the Dreyfus affair to Jewish influence.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage as a social institution is part of the family order he defended, so abolishing it contradicts his doctrine.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Transparency law is not in his sources; neutral.

local-production.rationale: Not part of his writing, though his localism gives a faint sympathy; neutral.

informal-organisation.rationale: He favored hierarchical leagues and a disciplined movement, not trust-based informal groups, so a mild disagreement.

religious-nation.rationale: Maurras was agnostic and defined the nation historically, though Catholicism is a criterion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: He was hostile to German hegemony and wanted France to be independent, so tributary deference contradicts his stance.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: His doctrine seeks regional liberties and local finances under a king, so some regional retention fits his decentralism.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Communism's property distinction is not his concern; he opposed collective ownership of production, so neutral on this formula.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Service delivery models are not addressed in his writing, so neutral.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: He was staunchly opposed to capitalism, and linked liberal modernity to decline, so he would not call it progressive.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: A socialist-feminist claim he would reject given his opposition to communism and egalitarianism.

socialized-care.rationale: Public provision of housework contradicts the traditional family order he defended; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic purism fits his classical, Latin-based cultural ideal weakly, but he is not documented on it, so neutral.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not addressed by Maurras, so neutral.

cooperative-communities.rationale: His organic local order resembles self-governing communities, but he rejected collectivist cooperatives and utopianism, so a mild disagreement.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not addressed, though he excluded some minorities from the nation, so neutral.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Maurras is described as staunchly opposed to both capitalism and communism, favoring corporatism as a third course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historical continuity is central to his nationalism, so historical ties are likely to count for claims; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not documented; he criticized Nazi racial policy.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not discussed in his sources; split between Catholic-conservative and classical-pagan attitudes, so neutral.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: He valued Catholicism as social order but was agnostic and not a theocrat, so it is a split matter.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: He opposed colonial expansion but not specified.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic legal doctrine irrelevant to his thought, so neutral.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: He was no theocrat, and valued Catholicism only politically, so he would not remove rulers for lack of religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He rejected democracy and favored hierarchy, so direct participation in decisions contradicts his doctrine.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: A modern critical theory contrary to his thought, so adherents would reject it.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; his traditionalist order would oppose such recognition.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; a Catholic-affiliated traditionalist outlook suggests opposition.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: He was an explicit man of the right who attacked the left and the Republic, so he would reject the claim that the split is obsolete.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept; his corporatist view was that trades give dignity, so he would not adopt it.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Legitimacy rested on reason not divine right.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: His movement backed the Church's public position and opposed laicist measures, so he would reject bans on religious dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic workplace law question, not addressed.

social-market-economy.rationale: A postwar German model not discussed by Maurras; corporatist protection overlaps but he disliked liberal markets, so neutral.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He valued the army and wanted France strong against Germany, so abolition is the opposite of his position.

rich-first.rationale: Not addressed; he did not argue for unequal development of regions, so neutral.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He backed alliances such as the one against Germany, so a neutral stance goes against his diplomacy.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not addressed in his writings; neutral.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Not addressed; nationalist sovereignty suggests sympathy but no source supports it, so neutral.

property-franchise.rationale: He rejected universal suffrage as such and favored corporate representation, but a property franchise is not documented, so neutral.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist claim contrary to his traditionalism; inferred disagreement.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept he would reject with the rest of Marxist theory.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: He denounced the republican press as venal, but his broader aim was not equal access, so neutral.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic and contrary to his preference for hierarchy over popular deliberation.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed in his writings; neutral.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Not discussed in his sources, though he was hostile to Jews and Protestants, so neutral.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Randomly selected deliberation fits a democratic idea he rejected, so adherents would reject it.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Not addressed; he valued the Church's unchanged order, but his personal agnosticism leaves this neutral.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; his anti-capitalism points to sympathy, but liberty was not his framework, so neutral.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from his traditional views of the army and society.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: He wanted a strong state with order and authority, so abolition contradicts his doctrine.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; he favored a unified nation under a king, so a mild disagreement.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: His Catholic and subsidiarist social order leaves local and church bodies a role, so a mild lean toward agreement.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; a hereditary monarch has no term limits, and he rejected elected politicians as a class, so he would at most be indifferent.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is a democratic device he rejected.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed, so neutral.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from traditional Catholic practice, which he valued as social order.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from his traditional family model, which kept authority in the father.

rent-control.rationale: Housing policy not addressed, so neutral.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed in his writings; inferred mild disagreement given his respect for property and inheritance.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed, so neutral.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Sovereignty and nation-first views suggest some sympathy, though he wanted allies, so a mild lean to agreement.

proportional-representation.rationale: He rejected party-based parliaments in favour of a king and councils of corporate and local representatives.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Revanchist nationalism toward Alsace-Lorraine suggests support; no explicit statement on other divided nations.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Maurras attacked finance and capitalism and favoured corporatism, but he defended property and hereditary order, so this is inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Maurras endorsed violence, war and political killing in the national interest, so no absolute bar on killing.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Maurras grounded France in a continuous inherited tradition from the Capetian monarchy, set against the Revolution's break with it.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from a traditionalist doctrine of fixed natural order; the sources do not discuss sex or gender.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from a hierarchical, hereditary and corporatist view that has no place for gender-identity politics.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from Action francaise's cult of national dead and Catholic civil religion, though Maurras himself was agnostic.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Maurras's politics-first empiricism treats politics as a science of order and national interest, though he saw Catholicism as social order.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from an integral nationalism centred on the French territory and state; not discussed directly.

culture-before-state.rationale: Politics first (politique d'abord) means restoring the monarchic state before anything else, the opposite of culture first.

god-not-male.rationale: Maurras valued Catholicism as social order rather than faith and kept traditional language; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from a traditionalist Catholic order that treats scripture and tradition as authoritative; not discussed.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Maurras treated Jews, Protestants, Freemasons and foreigners as anti-France and wanted them kept out of national life.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from his decentralist, provincial federal ideal, which favours historic provinces over new peoples' units.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from Maurras's corporatist and national-syndicalist leanings, which put unions inside an ordered national body rather than leaving them independent of it.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Action française was anti-socialist and rejected class struggle, so workers' own political power is not the test of a sound order.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from its decentralisation of administration to provinces and communes under the monarch, which favours local bodies running local services.

second-chamber.rationale: Maurras rejected parliament and elections; an advisory corporative council is more likely than a second elected chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from its defence of family property and hereditary order, which does not favour communal ownership of production.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Maurras wanted regional liberties granted and guarded by a hereditary monarch, not assemblies whose delegates only coordinate.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the central place of the family in Maurras's social order; not an explicit wage doctrine.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources say nothing and nothing in the doctrine commits adherents either way.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources say nothing and nothing in the doctrine commits adherents either way.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from its authoritarian state, which would not accept money beyond state control.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from its authoritarian, order-first politics; anachronistic and unstated.

person-over-state.rationale: Maurras subordinated the individual to the nation, treating liberal individual rights as a source of decay.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Maurras valued Catholicism as a social order and tradition, not as personal faith, so support is real but mild.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Maurras favoured regional liberties under the monarch, but the question about a national legislature's powers does not fit a monarchy without parliament.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources or doctrine bears on it.

dense-cities.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the doctrine bears on it, though Maurras idealised provincial rootedness.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Maurras rejected biological racism in favour of national and cultural exclusion, so organising by race is not his basis, though he named groups as 'anti-France'.

racial-pride.rationale: Maurras's pride was in the nation, its Catholic and Latin heritage, not in race as such.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from its militarist, nationalist outlook and its stress on national power and honour.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Maurras grounded the nation in heredity, territory, history and the state, not language alone, so a shared language does not make a nation. Inferred from his integral nationalism.

communal-electorates.rationale: Maurras rejected universal suffrage and wanted corporate representation, and treated Protestants and Jews as anti-France, so separate religious electorates do not fit. Inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Maurras treated foreigners and the 'four confederated states' as agents working against France, and was fixated on Germany weakening the country.

free-public-college.rationale: Not discussed; a corporatist, hierarchical order with elite education suggests no support for free tuition. Inferred.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Maurras's sources do not address environmental policy, and a dirigiste monarchy would rely on state direction rather than price mechanisms. Inferred.

future-generations.rationale: Maurras prized inheritance and continuity across generations as the basis of a nation, so a duty to hand on a good inheritance fits. Inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Maurras held traditional views on gender roles and was no champion of women in public life, so he would not give distinct feminine values more weight. Inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: Action française was militarist and nationalist and urged strong armaments against Germany, so it would reject cuts. Inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Maurras favoured a monarchy with continuity in foreign policy and disliked parliamentary control of diplomacy, so he would back confidential negotiation. Inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: Maurras is described as dirigiste and opposed to capitalism, so state control over capital movements is plausible. Inferred.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from Maurras's strong state and order-first politics; no source speaks to arms control.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Integral nationalism treats the army and national defence as supreme goods, so refusing orders in inter-state war runs against it.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The movement's corporatist and national-syndicalist leanings favoured organised trades and professional bodies settling conditions over liberal individual contracts.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Anachronistic; Maurras's sources do not discuss tax credits, and a paternal monarchy could go either way.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Maurras did not address borrowing rules; inferred as indifferent and so recorded neutral.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from nationalism that puts the national interest first and rejects internationalist schemes.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Maurras sought to overthrow the Republic by a coup de force and replace the regime with a monarchy, though keeping a strong administrative state; inferred as a mild yes.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from Maurras's insistence on a single hierarchical order under the king rather than open experimentation.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the doctrine's focus on politics over economics and its traditionalist view of land and patrimony.

sacred-nation.rationale: Maurras held the nation to be a hereditary patrimony of the dead and the living, a community greater than individuals.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources say nothing and no doctrine commits adherents.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Maurras blamed Paris-centred republican centralism for stifling provinces, but spoke of administrative decentralisation, not colonial exploitation; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Maurras rejected the abstract universal rights of man of the Revolution, though he held to a natural social order; inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from authoritarian, order-first views that favour state control over independent media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Maurras was an agnostic who valued Catholicism as the historic French order, not as one expression of a universal truth; he ranked Catholic France above other creeds.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from its corporatist and anti-liberal economics and its respect for the peasantry as an organic estate; the sources do not discuss price support.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic: inferred from its doctrine of national power and sovereignty ('politique d'abord'), which rejects unilateral disarmament.

workers-own-party.rationale: It rejected parties, parliamentarism and class struggle, wanting workers organised in national corporations under the monarchy rather than in their own party.

ban-fgm.rationale: Anachronistic: inferred from its hostility to foreign customs and its authoritarian order; the movement never addressed the practice.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Anachronistic: inferred; the movement was socially traditionalist but equal inheritance already existed in French law and it did not campaign to reverse it.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred: Maurras, a Provencal writer, defended regional languages within a decentralised France but held French unity paramount; the issue was not a doctrinal one.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred: it opposed liberal individualism and favoured a strong state authority, so private-law liability in place of agencies would not be its model.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: it favoured hereditary monarchy and traditional corporate bodies within France, but a national lawmaking role for customary chiefs is outside its tradition and colonial-era views.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred: it subordinates individual liberty to the collective national interest, but it had no environmental doctrine.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from its stress on order, authority and a strong state; it did not address sentencing policy.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred: it treated foreigners as 'anti-France' and demanded assimilation to French culture, though its main response was exclusion rather than a language requirement.

missingStatements.text: The nation's enemies include groups within it, such as religious or ethnic minorities, who should be treated as foreign to the nation.
missingStatements.rationale: Maurras grouped Jews, Protestants, Freemasons and foreigners as the 'four confederated states' of anti-France, and urged state action against them.

missingStatements.text: A country's real communities of family, locality and trade matter more than its formal political institutions.
missingStatements.rationale: The pays réel against the pays légal is a central Maurrassian distinction.

notes: Maurras was agnostic until near his death and valued Catholicism politically, which led the Vatican to condemn the movement in 1926-27 (lifted in 1939). Many answers on modern issues are inferred at low confidence.
